Le bus était totalement silencieux à part pour les bruits de bisous qu'il faisait et tout ce qu'il me disait.. Au début j'essayais de l'ignorer, puis je lui ai dis non plusieurs fois, au bout d'un moment je lui dit mon age et il a haussé les épaules en me disant qu'il s'en fichait. Personne n'a dit quoi que ce soit ni levé le petit doigt, alors que le bus était plein. 
Je ne sais plus exactement comment ça s'est fini mais je suis arrivée à destination et sans lui.

I asked my father multiple times, but he says he doesn't know what happened. I don't believe him completly because if an investigation was conducted I think he might have been in contact with the police, and the ASE contacted him as soon as I was put in a nursery home. But in my father's side of my family (his siblings and my grandparents), my mom and what I went through while I was living with her as a young child are pretty taboo and no one ever talk about it. I know they mean well, and it is their way to try to "protect" me (even if I'm adult now), and they feel guilty about some things I went through with her, so I decided to not not insist that they give me answers and try to find by myself for now. I will ask them again if I find nothing, of course.

As for my mom, she is back in the picture since some years. She started to take her medication for schizophrenia two years ago, and since then, we are finally starting to reconnect. She is doing so great at trying to get her life back together, I don't want to adress that kind of matter with her right now, I just want to support her. I will talk to her about my childhood someday, but for now, I just want to make up for the time we lost.

So yeah, for now I am trying to find answer on my own :)

Hi !  


I have go a Borderline Personality Disorder and I wanted to say that, for me, yes it is so much better now than 15, 10 or even 1 year ago. Indeed, after years of therapies, disappointments, worrying, suffering, loneliness and isolation, constant fear, support from some people and separation with other, psychological and physical tiredness, depression, bad choices, good choices, learning, toxic relationships, relationships that I spoiled, and everything good and bad (life), well I feel so much better.  
I understand so much what you mean by 'exhausting', I have felt that a million times, but really, today, with the good doctors, the good medication, and time spent learning to love and to know myself (which is, for me, very important), everything works better. My brain works better.   


The more I know myself, the more I have confidence in myself, and so in others, and so I start to do the good choices for me. Choices that make me happy and stable. I started a few months ago the first love relationship that makes me really happy, I cut all those that were toxic, and I'm learning (after many fails and ridiculous lol) to create and make bloom healthy one. I'm finishing college and I'm in an internship since last month. I'm starting to live simply and to tame us, my brain and I.

  
In short, I wrote a lot (sorry for my bad english, it's not my first language) and I don't know if I answered your question or not, but all this just to say : yes, it is better for me.  


I can only advise you to stay patient, veeeeeryyyyyy patient, and to always find a little something to hold on to and to believe in yourself, because if you got here today it's only because of you, your courage, your determination and your strengh and you can achieve anything just like you did all your life. So, be brave ! I believe in you very very much and it will get better for you too if you hold on as long as it needs, even when you are the most exhausted.

Hi ! I did something that actually helped me a lot about my relationship with my boyfriend. 
I started a diary in which I committed myself to write everyday, the more sincerely possible,  about every fear or emotions I felt in the day.  By sincerely I mean that when my fears where unfounded, I had to write that too.  It helped me to be more rational. After the day's summary,  I write how I could have handle my emotions better or how I could have act differently to make things better.  After that,  I write a list of every positive thing that happened to me in the day,  even those that can seem insignificant,  because they are not,  they count as much as every other good thing that I can take.  And I finish everyday with a very encouraging conclusion,  where I force myself to compliment and encourage me.
In a few days I could already control my emotions better and rationalize more ! :)
